title: The First Chapter
hook: Write the beginning twice, apart, before either voice can steer it.
steps: 10 quiet minutes. Five lines each: where it begins for you, and a different day is allowed; what you were unsure of; one detail later tellings have polished; what you guessed the other person felt; one fact you still do not know, which may stay private.
One person reads the five lines. The listener does not correct a name or improve a line. Private marks only: same memory, news to me, I remember it differently. Then switch.
Now talk. Say both beginnings and what each is counting. One curious question for the news. Set disagreements side by side, and do not average them.
ending: Optional: one agreed fact and one uncertainty you will leave in. Or name that uncertainty and stop.
pass: Skip any stretch you do not want replayed. No reason is required. You may stop after one scene.
safety: Stop if a live argument about faithfulness is waiting. Have it in plain time.

title: The Moments You Didn’t Know Mattered
hook: A small act you carried at a size the giver never heard. Not a performance of gratitude.
steps: 8 quiet minutes. Up to five small items: a sentence, a chore, a look, a restraint, a practical save. Three should be smaller than a gift or a trip. One honest item is enough.

Trade one at a time: where you were, what they did, and why it stayed. The receiver lets it land and does not improve the story. One curious question. They may take a minute. A different memory does not cancel yours.
Switch one for one. No matching size is required. Two spoken and the rest private is complete.
Agreed pairs only, in two columns: what was done, and what it meant. Shrink a swollen sentence back to the gesture.
ending: Read the columns once at their actual size. Leave the week alone.
pass: Stop early if you want. Skip a third person's secret, and a sexual moment you have not both agreed to discuss.

title: Our Greatest Hits
hook: Four columns. A funny story does not have to be the meaningful one.
steps: Headings: funniest, most romantic, unexpected, meaningful. Quietly write a slug for each you have: place, the turn, why it plays. Empty stays empty.
Take one column at a time. A story may sit in two only if you both agree. Tell the place, the turn, and why it still plays.
The listener asks for one extra detail, names what landed, and saves their own story for their turn. If you split on whether it was funny, write both. No vote.
Mark keepers you both will retell, one is enough, plus one detail you will stop sanding. Read the headings, empties included.
ending: Then stop, before the hits become a second dinner.
pass: A nomination can move to a private margin with no case to argue. You may pass a column.
safety: Humiliating a partner, or a friend who is not here, stays off. Stories about sex, bodies, or family need a yes from both.

title: The Moment I Saw You Differently
hook: Four beats: the smaller picture, the place, the detail that broke it, the wider one.
steps: 5 quiet minutes. Sketch the smaller picture without scolding your past self, one scene, the detail that refused to fit, and the wider picture: warmer, stranger, sadder, or more accurate. Not a diagnosis. No detail means pass.
Speak the four beats. A minute of quiet before the listener talks.

They reflect the change, and may add how it felt inside the scene. They do not grind down the old picture, sweeten it, or perform the quality. A missing memory does not erase the seeing. They need not agree.
Switch to a different episode. Close with one line each: what you know now that you could not have known at the start.
ending: Then stop. A tour of every misreading is a different week.
pass: Pass an accusation or an open injury, unless you both want that scene. No third person's secret.

title: The Unspoken Thank-You
hook: Finish one thanks that lost the race with the week. The cost may be wrong.
steps: 8 minutes apart. Three sentences: what they did; what you think it cost them, as a guess; what changed for you. Name the act.
Read. The receiver takes it in, and may correct the cost with care. They do not joke it away or answer with a thanks in the same breath.
Switch. Size and era need not match. No unpaid thanks you believe is a finished turn: say you looked.
ending: Ask once if a sentence may be kept. A no still leaves the spoken thanks complete. Then stop.
pass: If resentment is still tangled in it, pick a smaller finished act or postpone. You may decline a thanks that sweetens a hard period.
safety: Do not thank a partner for harm endured, silence, or unfair work treated as a gift. A request disguised as thanks gets cut.
